subject: wright-brothers
title: Why the Wrights Won: R&D Lessons, 1899–1905
summary: Problem decomposition, distrust of inherited data, and capital efficiency.

keys.prompt: In what order did the Wrights attack flight's three problems?
keys.answer: Control first (1899 wing-warping kite), then lift data (1901 wind tunnel), propulsion last (1903).

keys.prompt: How could a cruder, weaker engine than Langley's suffice?
keys.answer: Efficient wings and propellers meant less power was needed.

keys.prompt: What's the "demo is not product" lesson from 1903 to 1905?
keys.answer: 1903 proved powered flight in seconds; a practical aircraft took two more years, until Wilbur's 39-minute closed-course flight in 1905.

cards.title: Funding vs. method
cards.text: Langley had War Department underwriting, Smithsonian prestige, and a stronger engine. The Wrights had a Dayton bicycle shop and a four-year R&D program. Which advantage actually mattered?

cards.question: Langley had government funding and a stronger engine. The Wrights had a bike shop. Which advantage do you think decided the race?
cards.reveal: Method. The Wrights sequenced the problem (control, then lift data, then propulsion) and their efficient wings and propellers needed less power. Langley "relied on brute power."

cards.title: Decompose the problem
cards.text: Flight needs lift, control, and propulsion. The Wrights sequenced them: control first (the 1899 wing-warping kite), then lift data (the 1901 wind tunnel), propulsion last (1903). Per the Park Service, Langley "relied on brute power" to keep theoretically stable machines aloft.
cards.example: The Wrights' premise was that a pilot must actively fly the machine. Their 1,000-plus glides made them the first true pilots before they ever added an engine.

cards.title: Distrust inherited data
cards.text: The 1900 and 1901 gliders produced substantially less lift than their calculations predicted. They built a wind tunnel in fall 1901 whose instruments measured lift and drag coefficients, the exact terms in the equations they doubted.
cards.example: The 1902 glider, designed from their own data, made 700 to 1,000 flights. That is model-versus-reality reconciliation before scaling.

why.q: Why measure lift and drag coefficients specifically?
why.a: They were the exact terms in the equations the Wrights doubted. Measuring them fixed the model instead of just the glider.

cards.title: Capital efficiency
cards.text: They chose Kitty Hawk after asking the U.S. Weather Bureau about strong, steady winds and sand. Finding no light enough commercial engine, they built a 12-horsepower one with mechanic Charles Taylor. It was cruder and weaker than Langley's, but efficient wings and propellers meant less power was needed.
cards.example: The propellers, designed from tunnel data as rotating wings, are called one of their most original, purely scientific achievements.

cards.title: Demo is not product
cards.text: December 17, 1903: 12 seconds and 120 feet, then 852 feet in 59 seconds. A gust then wrecked the Flyer. Refined aircraft followed in 1904 and 1905. On October 5, 1905, Wilbur flew 39 minutes and 24.5 miles over a closed course.

cards.prompt: Gutenberg integrated existing technologies and solved one hard sub-problem himself (interchangeable type). What's the parallel with the Wrights?
cards.model: Both integrated existing pieces and built in-house the one piece nobody could supply (the type mold; the wind-tunnel data and a light engine) before scaling.

cards.question: The Wrights' edge was a tight build-test-learn loop and taking nothing on authority. Where is your organization's "published data" quietly wrong, and what would a cheap wind tunnel look like?
nudges: Which assumption do you inherit and never test?
What is the smallest experiment that would falsify it?

questions.q: Which achievement does the Park Service call one of the Wrights' most original and purely scientific?

options.text: Designing the first efficient airplane propeller from their tunnel data
options.why: Right. They treated the propeller as a rotating wing.

options.text: Building the most powerful engine of the era
options.why: Their engine was cruder and less powerful than Langley's.
Not highlighted that way. The propeller is.
That was Langley's backing, not an achievement of the Wrights.

questions.q: What did the 1901 wind tunnel instruments measure?

options.text: Lift and drag coefficients on model wing shapes
options.why: Yes, the terms in the lift and drag equations they doubted.
The engine came in 1903. The tunnel was about wing data.
They got site information from the Weather Bureau. The tunnel tested model wings.

questions.q: When did a Wright aircraft show clearly practical, sustained flight?

options.why: Right. The 1903 flights proved it possible; 1905 made it practical.
That flight lasted 12 seconds. A milestone, not yet a practical aircraft.
Wilbur's attempt that day stalled after leaving the rail.
The kite tested control and carried no pilot.
